subject.title: refactor(auth): harden CLI forwarding proposal boundary

question: Should OpenClaw establish this generic provider-to-CLI-backend auth-forwarding contract, and must it land only with the first real consumer and removal of the current Gemini-only raw-credential bridge?
rationale: The choice determines which plugin boundary may transform canonical credentials and whether OpenClaw creates a lasting compatibility contract; source inspection cannot safely choose that security and product boundary without owner intent.

options.title: Require complete integration
options.body: Approve the minimized direction only as one change with a provider hook, real CLI consumer, private-bridge removal, compatibility coverage, and live proof.

options.title: Keep provider-specific bridges
options.body: Reject a generic contract and retain credential staging within each bundled provider/backend owner.

options.title: Land internal groundwork
options.body: Merge the unused validator now and defer its consumer and permanent API direction.

recommendation.title: Require complete integration
recommendation.body: Approve the minimized direction only as one change with a provider hook, real CLI consumer, private-bridge removal, compatibility coverage, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current `prepareExecution` boundary and explicit temporary Gemini exception, making him the closest available owner for its permanent replacement.
